newsitem.title: USA: Comerica to eliminate about 1,890 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Comerica to eliminate about 1,890 jobs.

text.p: Comerica Inc said it expects to eliminate about 1,890 jobs as part of a comprehensive streamlining effort designed to slash costs and boost revenues by $110 million annually by the first half of 1998.
Comerica said it incurred a $90 million pre-tax restructuring charge in the fourth quarter, which reduced earnings per share for the period by $0.54.

"Regrettably, as we streamline processes and eliminate redundancies, a number of employees throughout the corporation will be displaced," Comerica Chairman Eugene Miller. "To assist these employees, we have put in place an enhanced severance plan with outplacement services to help their transition."
However, Comerica said the actual number of employees to be laid off may be less than 1,890 because of normal attrition, a hiring freeze and reinvestment actions.

Comerica, with $34 billion in assets at the end of 1996, said the third phase of its "Direction 2000" restructuring efforts also includes a number of other initiatives to reduce costs and enhance revenues. They include:
-- Eliminating one-third of paper forms and replacing them with electronic forms.
-- Simplifying the referral and delivery of investment services.
-- Empowering branch employees with additional levels of authority, and reducing their clerical responsibilities, so they can serve customers better.
-- Automating loan documentation to accelerate customer response times.
-- Reducing the documentation required to open a new account.

Comerica said the charge associated with the restructuring actions held its fourth quarter 1996 net income to $60.8 million, or $0.52 a share, compared with year-earlier net income of $106.5 million, or $0.92 a share.
